title: Quantum Computing gets Wedbush backing for photonics opportunity despite profitability questions
excerpt: Quantum Computing Inc. (NASDAQ:QUBT), the US photonics technology company, delivered third-quarter revenue above expectations, but Wedbush maintained its...
content:
Quantum Computing Inc. (NASDAQ:QUBT), the US photonics technology company, delivered third-quarter revenue above expectations, but Wedbush maintained its Neutral rating and $12 price target.

Revenue for the three months to September 2026 reached $9.5 million, beating the Wall Street consensus estimate of $7.2 million and Wedbush's $9.2 million forecast.

The result also exceeded the $9.2 million generated during the first half of 2026, highlighting the contribution from recent acquisitions.

Gross margin improved to 4.5%, compared with negative 21% in the second quarter, although it remained below the 16.3% consensus estimate.

Earnings per share showed a loss of $0.07, two cents wider than the market forecast but one cent better than Wedbush expected.

The broker described the revenue performance as solid but said the company still needed to provide a clearer roadmap towards profitability.

The LSI, NuCrypt and NHanced acquisitions contributed $8.8 million of quarterly revenue, leaving organic revenue of approximately $700,000, up from $450,000 in the previous quarter.

Operating expenses totalled $29 million, including approximately $1 million of acquisition-related costs, with management expecting the underlying expense level to provide a reasonable indication for the fourth quarter.

Interest income of $13 million offset almost half of operating expenses, while cash and investments remained broadly unchanged at approximately $1.3 billion, with no debt.

The company's backlog fell to $39.1 million from $42.5 million, reflecting uneven contract awards and strong conversion of existing orders during the quarter.

On the technology front, Quantum Computing announced Dirac-3S, a next-generation optimisation machine supporting up to 9,980 variables, with its first shipment expected in the fourth quarter.

Commercial progress included signing INmune Bio as its first pharmaceutical and biotechnology customer, alongside a framework agreement with Hamad Bin Khalifa University covering cloud access to its Dirac-3 system.

Management also said it had achieved its 2024 to 2026 roadmap objectives and was shifting its focus towards manufacturing expansion.

This includes a planned $70 million to $80 million expansion of Fab 2 at NHanced, aimed at increasing production capacity.

Wedbush lowered its fourth-quarter revenue forecast to $10.5 million from $10.7 million previously expected by the market, taking its 2026 estimate to $29.2 million from $34 million.

The broker cited uncertainty around order timing and deliveries, with management declining to provide formal revenue guidance.

However, Wedbush raised its 2027 and 2028 revenue forecasts to $54 million and $114.9 million respectively, reflecting stronger expected contributions from acquisitions.

It also adopted a more gradual gross margin recovery, lowering its 2027 forecast to 15% from 33.8%.

The broker's $12 price target is based on a discounted cash flow valuation using a 26% weighted average cost of capital and 5% terminal growth rate.

Wedbush's central concern remains whether photonics will emerge as the leading quantum computing technology and whether Quantum Computing can establish itself among the best-positioned suppliers.

The broker sees a credible opportunity in photonic components and advanced packaging, even if the company ultimately falls behind competitors in quantum computing performance.
